messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High 5xx rate and streaming disconnects detected for /v1/stream (prod, us-west-2). Error spike started ~10:12 UTC. Paging on-call. Severity: P1. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood-inference/internal/streams?span=10m

maya_oncall: acked. jumping in. seeing client cancels + chunked encoding truncation in traces.

maya_oncall: quick check — are we seeing gateway 502/504 vs runtime 5xx?

tim_sre: root shows a surge of 502s at the gateway layer (nginx LB) at same time as increased backend timeouts. logs: `502 gateway response: upstream prematurely closed connection` repeated.

ryan_backend: adding context: the runtime logs show `client canceled` during last-chunk flush for some requests. KV cache pressure spike on serving nodes around same time.

maya_oncall: ok — sounds like two correlated signals: gateway proxy resets + backend chunked flush failures. Impact: some streaming clients see partial responses then stream closed, others get 5xx. Customer ops pinged. @lee_csm please chime in on customer impact.

lee_csm: getting reports from two enterprise customers complaining of truncated responses and apps retrying -> duplicate outputs. One customer reported an outage window ~ 5-7m starting at 10:13 UTC. They're asking for ETA.

sre-manager: escalation: bring in ingress team and prepare a fallback model route. Also consider disabling persistent keepalive or lowering buffer thresholds on gateway as live mitigation.

edge-ingress: looking at LB metrics — CPU on the frontend proxies spiked, connection pool exhaustion on some nodes. I see many `RST` events to backend during the spike. Possible upstream node OOM or thread-starvation.

maya_oncall: mitigation plan (live): 1) fail traffic from overloaded edge nodes -> route to standby edge pool; 2) switch streaming route to paged non-chunked fallback for customers with high error rates; 3) bump backend timeout to allow chunk flush until root cause identified.

tim_sre: doing 1) now: marking nodes out of rotation in the LB. Command:```bash
# mark node out
curl -X POST "https://infra-api/edges/pool/rotation" -d '{"node_id":"edge-47","action":"drain"}'
```

tim_sre: 1) done for two hot nodes, traffic drained. 502 rate dropped from 18% -> 9% in 90s.

maya_oncall: 2) applying fallback route: update route /v1/stream -> /v1/stream-paged for affected tenant ids. This will break streaming semantics but restores completion. Patch applied via routing config.```

deploy-bot: Deployment started: routing-change-2517002468 -> green.

ryan_backend: rolling a small config change to increase backend keepalive buffers and log chunk-finalization more verbosely. Patch:```yaml
runtime:
  http:
    max_buffer_size: 8mb
    chunk_flush_timeout_ms: 1500
```

maya_oncall: 3) bumping backend timeouts by +2s to tolerate GC/flush. Watch for cost/latency regressions.

tim_sre: after rotations + route fallback + timeout bump, errors stabilized to ~1.2% 5xx and client-cancel traces reduced. Still seeing occasional chunk-truncation traces tied to specific model-serving pods.

ryan_backend: dug into pod logs: there are `SIGPIPE` and `write: connection reset by peer` entries around the time of peak. The runtime's KV cache eviction was very noisy (eviction churn). Suspect memory pressure triggered by large sequence requests + continuous batching causing eviction thrash.

maya_oncall: good detective work. next steps: 1) pin heavy seq-length models to dedicated pool to stop churn; 2) add cache metrics alarms; 3) create follow-up incident for postmortem.

lee_csm: Customers notified with interim mitigation: switched to paged fallback and we have targeted retries. They want root cause + timeline. I'll send a short update: "We've mitigated the immediate impact by routing affected workloads to a non-streaming fallback and draining overloaded ingress nodes. Engineering is investigating the root cause and will follow up with a postmortem."

sre-manager: action items assigned in incident ticket #INC-251700: 1) root cause analysis (ryan + tim), 2) infra scaling rules update (edge-ingress), 3) add cache eviction alarms (runtime team), 4) runbook update for streaming silent-close.

tim_sre: temporary monitoring query I pushed to reduce noise:```promql
sum by(status) (rate(http_responses_total{route="/v1/stream"}[2m]))
```

maya_oncall: all participants please confirm any ongoing customer-facing elevated errors. If none, we'll move to recovery phase in 15m and start a conference bridge for RCA.

ryan_backend: confirming no new customers reporting after fallback. Logs still show a handful of client cancels but at non-impacting rate.

edge-ingress: LB pool scaling rules updated to increase baseline pool by 20% during daytime roll windows. Also scheduled hotfix to backpressure long-lived streaming connections if queue depth > 80%.

maya_oncall: starting postmortem draft and will include timeline + mitigation steps. Tagging it as P1->P2 after stabilization. Thanks everyone for fast coordination. :thumbsup:
